c.title: Proposal 2026-1
c.pre: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
c.q: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?

c.title: Proposal 2026-2
c.pre: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
c.q:
The proposal would:

• Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them.

• Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them.

• Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: Fire Operating Millage Proposal
c.q: Shall the annual tax rate limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution be increased for said Township by up to 1.0 mill ($1 per $1000 on Taxable value) for the period 2027 – 2028, inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds to the Whiteford Township Fire Department to be used for general operations including wages, utilities, salaries and benefits of firefighters, and maintenance to the fire department buildings and equipment? The estimated revenue for the first year of the levy, if the proposition is approved, shall be approximately $321,315.35.

c.title: Fire Services Special Assessment Proposal
c.q: Shall the City of Milan, Counties of Washtenaw and Monroe, Michigan, be authorized to establish a city-wide special assessment district pursuant to Act 33, Public Acts of Michigan, 1951, as amended, to raise money by special assessment for the purpose of paying certain costs and expenses of fire services, including maintenance and operations, fire motor vehicles, apparatus, equipment, and housing?

c.title: Fire Protection Proposal
c.q: Shall the annual tax rate limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution be increased, and shall the Township of Bedford be authorized to levy an additional millage of 1.00 mills ($1.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value), upon the taxable real and tangible personal property within the Township of Bedford, Monroe County, Michigan, each year for a period of ten (10) years to be collected annually beginning in 2028 and continuing through 2037, inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds to the Bedford Township Fire Department to be used for acquiring, improving and maintaining Fire Department equipment, vehicles, buildings and apparatus? The estimated revenue for the first year of the levy, if the proposition is approved, shall be approximately $1,580,439.00.

c.title: Road and Bridges Millage Renewal
c.q: Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Dundee Township of 1.0 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) per year which is due to expire in 2027 be renewed for a period of 10 years, commencing in 2028 through 2037 inclusive, for the purpose of funding for the improvement of Township roads and bridges; and which if approved will raise in the first year of levy estimated revenue of $465,734.15.

c.title: Summerfield Schools Sinking Fund Millage Proposal
c.q: Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Summerfield Schools, Monroe County, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 2 mills ($2.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 4 years, 2027 to 2030, inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the construction or repair of school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $509,704?

c.title: BRITTON DEERFIELD SCHOOLS SINKING FUND MILLAGE PROPOSAL
c.q: Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Britton Deerfield Schools, Lenawee and Monroe Counties, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 2 mills ($2.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 4 years, 2027 to 2030, inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the purchase of real estate for sites for, and the construction or repair of, school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and for all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $539,102?

c.title: Village of Estral Beach Flood Control Millage
c.q:
Proposition to authorize the Village of Estral Beach to extend the expiring millage and levy a property tax of 2 mills for a total of four ( 4) years for the purpose of maintaining and hardening the Village's flood control measures.

Shall the Village of Estral Beach, Monroe County, levy a 2-mills property tax and place it on the property tax roll for years 2027, 2028, 2029 , and 2030, which will raise in the first year of such levy an estimated revenue of forty three thousand dollars ($43,000) for the purpose of maintaining and hardening (e.g., install steel walls) of the Village owned flood control measures .

c.title: Village of Estral Beach Supplemental Flood Control Millage
c.q:
Proposition to authorize the Village of Estral Beach to extend the expiring millage and levy a property tax of 2-mills for a total of four ( 4) years for the purpose of improving and maintaining Village berms, levees, ditch system, pumps, and other flood control measures as needed.

Shall the Village of Estral Beach, Monroe County, Michigan, levy an additional 2-mills property tax and place it on the property tax roll for the years 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030 which will raise in the first year of such levy an estimated revenue of forty three thousand dollars ($43,000) for the purpose of improving and maintaining Village berms, levees, ditch system, pumps, and other flood control measures as needed.

c.title: Jefferson Schools Bond Proposal
c.q:
Shall Jefferson Schools, Monroe County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty-Eight Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($28,700,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, in one or more series, for the purpose of:

remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings, including roof replacements and safety and security improvements; and preparing, developing, and improving sites?

The following is for informational purposes only:

The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 2.00 mills ($2.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds of any series may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is twenty (20) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 1.99 mills ($1.99 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).

(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)

c.title: Renewal of Township Fire Equipment, Operation & Maintenance
c.q: Shall the Township of Ash, County of Monroe, Michigan, renew a levy of .4839 mill property tax and place it upon the property tax rolls for the years 2027, 2028, 2029, 2030, for the purpose of purchasing, acquiring, maintaining and operating fire trucks, equipment and materials and expenses for the Ash Township Fire Department? Based on the current taxable value, it is estimated that this .4839 mill property tax will generate approximately $207,887.17 in the first calendar year of the millage.
